images.title: Hippocratic oath fragment on papyrus (P. Oxy. 2547)
images.caption: A fragment of the Hippocratic oath written on papyrus in the 3rd century AD, catalogued as Oxyrhynchus papyrus no. 2547 (verso). The Wellcome Collection holds it under library reference WMS 5754.
images.alt: Tall, torn brown papyrus fragment covered in lines of Greek handwriting
images.creator: Unknown scribe, Roman Egypt; photograph Wellcome Collection (L0029601)
images.locationNote: Find-spot: Oxyrhynchus (el-Bahnasa), Egypt; the papyrus is now in the Wellcome Collection, London
images.rightsEvidence: Commons file page Licensing section: "This file is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license." (license template short name: CC BY 4.0). Description: "Fragment of Hippocratic oath: (verso). Oxyrhynchus papyrus no. 2547"; "Library reference: WMS 5754 Photo number: L0029601".

images.title: Confession to a bishop, from Dirc van Delft's Table of Christian Faith
images.caption: This folio from Walters manuscript W.171, painted in Utrecht between 1400 and 1404 for Albert, Duke of Bavaria and Count of Holland, depicts a confession to a bishop. It belongs to Dirc van Delft's Table of Christian Faith, ink and pigments on parchment.
images.alt: Manuscript page in Middle Dutch script with a gilded initial D enclosing a mitred bishop seated beside a veiled penitent, two men waiting behind, framed by a floral border
images.creator: Dirc van Delft (text) and unknown illuminator, Utrecht
images.creditLine: Walters Art Museum, Baltimore (W.171, fol. 114v) / Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
images.locationNote: Place of creation: Utrecht, Netherlands (per the record); now in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore
images.rightsEvidence: Commons file page Licensing section: "This file was provided to Wikimedia Commons by the Walters Art Museum as part of a cooperation project. All artworks in the photographs are in public domain due to age. The photographs of two-dimensional objects are also in the public domain." License template: Public domain. Accession number W.171.114V; "Place of creation Utrecht, Netherlands"; "Date between 1400 and 1404".

images.title: Tractate Bava Batra, Bomberg Talmud (Venice, 1522)
images.caption: An opening of Tractate Bava Batra of the Babylonian Talmud, printed in Venice by Daniel Bomberg in 1522. By number of printed pages Bava Batra is the longest tractate in the Bomberg Talmud, because Rashi's concise commentary stops at folio 29a and the less succinct commentary of his grandson Rashbam takes over.
images.alt: Open printed Hebrew volume showing two pages, each with a block of Talmud text surrounded by columns of commentary
images.creator: Daniel Bomberg (printer), Venice
images.creditLine: Wikimedia Commons (public domain; photograph via Sotheby's)
images.rightsEvidence: Commons file page Licensing section: "This is a faithful photographic reproduction of a two-dimensional, public domain work of art. ... This work is in the public domain in the United States because it was published (or registered with the U.S. Copyright Office) before January 1, 1931." Description: "Babylonian Talmud, Tractate Bava Batra, Venice: Daniel Bomberg, 1522."

images.title: The Hippocratic oath written in the shape of a cross
images.caption: In this twelfth-century Byzantine manuscript the Hippocratic oath is written out in the form of a cross, relating it visually to Christian ideas. The scan reproduces a photograph from the Vatican Library published in Ira M. Rutkow's Surgery: An Illustrated History (1993).
images.alt: Stained parchment page of small Greek minuscule script, the central text block laid out in the shape of a cross
images.creator: Unknown Byzantine scribe
images.creditLine: Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana (photograph) / Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
images.upstreamArchive: Wikimedia Commons (scan of a Vatican Library photograph)
images.locationNote: Vatican Library, Vatican City, where the manuscript is held (the record credits 'Foto de la Biblioteca Vaticana'); place of writing not stated
images.rightsEvidence: Commons file page Licensing section: "This file is in the public domain because it is a mere mechanical scan or photocopy of a public domain original ... This work is in the public domain in the United States because it was published (or registered with the U.S. Copyright Office) before January 1, 1931." Also tagged Public Domain Mark 1.0. Description: "Twelfth-century Byzantine manuscript the oath was written out in the form of a cross, relating it visually to Christian ideas".

images.title: Sir Edward Coke, engraved by Simon van de Passe
images.caption: Portrait engraving of the jurist Edward Coke by Simon van de Passe, published in London by Compton Holland; the Rijksmuseum dates it between 1605 and 1647. The oval frame carries Coke's name and office in Latin, his coat of arms and books in the corners, and a six-line Latin poem of praise below.
images.alt: Engraved oval portrait of a bearded man in a ruff and chain of office, framed by Latin lettering, coats of arms and books
images.creator: Simon van de Passe (engraver); Compton Holland (publisher)
images.locationNote: Place of production per the Rijksmuseum record: London (city-level coordinates)
images.rightsEvidence: Commons file page Licensing section: "This file is made available under the Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication." Rijksmuseum description on the page: "Copyright: Publiek domein"; "prentmaker: Simon van de Passe ... uitgever: Compton Holland ... Plaats vervaardiging: Londen Datering: 1605 - 1647".

images.title: John Wilkes, Esq., etched by William Hogarth
images.caption: William Hogarth's etched and engraved portrait of John Wilkes, dated 16 May 1763 in the Metropolitan Museum's record (first state of two). Its lettering reads "Drawn from the Life and Etch'd in Aquafortis by Willm Hogarth", and papers marked North Briton Number 45 and Number 17 lie on the table beside the sitter.
images.alt: Etching of a grinning, squinting man in a wig seated on a chair, holding a staff topped by a cap labelled LIBERTY; papers marked North Briton Number 45 and Number 17 lie on the table beside him
images.creator: William Hogarth
images.creditLine: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Sarah Lazarus, 1891 (CC0)
images.locationNote: Published in London, where Hogarth worked (city-level coordinates); impression now at the Met, New York
images.rightsEvidence: Met Collection API /public/collection/v1/objects/392613 returns "isPublicDomain": true (Met Open Access, CC0); "objectDate": "May 16, 1763"; "medium": "Etching and engraving; first state of two"; accession 91.1.8. images.title: Charles Pratt, Baron Camden, drawn by Francesco Bartolozzi
images.caption: Oval portrait in black and red chalk of Charles Pratt, Baron Camden (later 1st Earl Camden), by the engraver Francesco Bartolozzi; the Metropolitan Museum dates it between 1764 and 1802. The drawing was formerly attributed to John Singleton Copley.
images.alt: Oval chalk drawing on tan paper of an older man's head in a curled wig, turned three-quarters to the right
images.creator: Francesco Bartolozzi (formerly attributed to John Singleton Copley)
images.creditLine: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Morris K. Jesup Fund, 1955 (CC0)
images.locationNote: Sitter's seat of work: London, where Pratt sat as Chief Justice of the Common Pleas in Entick v Carrington (1765); place of drawing not recorded
images.rightsEvidence: Met Collection API /public/collection/v1/objects/338158 returns "isPublicDomain": true (Met Open Access, CC0); "objectDate": "1764–1802"; "medium": "Black and red chalk, varnished"; constituents include "Formerly attributed to John Singleton Copley". images.title: Plan of Jeremy Bentham's Panopticon
images.caption: Elevation, section and half-plan of Jeremy Bentham's Panopticon, as printed in The Works of Jeremy Bentham, vol. IV (1843), pp. 172-3, from the original design of 1791. Cells marked A ring the building's outer wall around a central core.
images.alt: Architectural drawing of a multi-storey circular building: exterior elevation and cut-away section above, a semicircular floor plan of radiating cells around a central tower below
images.creator: Jeremy Bentham (design; drawn by Willey Reveley)
images.creditLine: The Works of Jeremy Bentham, vol. IV (1843) / Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
images.upstreamArchive: Wikimedia Commons (scan of The Works of Jeremy Bentham, 1843)
images.locationNote: London, where Bentham lived and worked (city-level coordinates); the Panopticon was never built to this plan
images.rightsEvidence: Commons file page Licensing section: "This work is in the public domain in its country of origin and other countries and areas where the copyright term is the author's life plus 100 years or fewer." Also tagged Public Domain Mark 1.0. Description: "Plan of the Panopticon"; "Date 1843 (originally 1791)"; "Source The works of Jeremy Bentham vol. IV, 172-3"; Author Jeremy Bentham (1748-1832).

images.title: The Bill of Rights, as proposed by Congress in 1789
images.caption: The Bill of Rights dated 25 September 1789: twelve articles of amendment to the United States Constitution proposed by the Congress 'begun and held at the City of New-York', of which articles three to twelve became part of the Constitution. On this document the First Amendment is 'Article the third', so today's Fourth Amendment appears as 'Article the sixth'.
images.alt: Faded handwritten parchment headed 'Congress of the United States', with a preamble and a column of numbered articles below
images.creator: First Federal Congress of the United States
images.creditLine: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NAID 1408042), public domain
images.upstreamArchive: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
images.locationNote: Federal Hall, New York City, where the First Congress sat in 1789; the document is now in the National Archives, Washington, D.C.
images.rightsEvidence: Commons file page Permission/Licensing: "This work is in the public domain in the United States because it is a work prepared by an officer or employee of the United States Federal Government as part of that person's official duties under the terms of Title 17, Chapter 1, Section 105 of the US Code." Source: "This media is available in the holdings of the National Archives and Records Administration, cataloged under the National Archives Identifier (NAID) 1408042." Note: the Commons description says the ten articles became part of the Constitution "in 1794"; ratification was completed in 1791, so the caption avoids that date.

images.title: Hollerith's electrical counting machines at the 1890 US census
images.caption: Scientific American illustrated the Hollerith electric tabulating machine in use for the 1890 United States census in its issue of 30 August 1890. A clerk reads a schedule at the machine while stacks of punched cards pile up beside her and more operators work behind.
images.alt: Engraving of a woman seated at a desk-like tabulating machine with a panel of dials, a sheet in her hand and stacks of cards beside her, other clerks working in the background
images.creator: Artist not credited; Scientific American
images.creditLine: Scientific American, 30 August 1890 / Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
images.locationNote: Washington, D.C., where the Census Office tabulated the 1890 count (city-level coordinates); the magazine was published in New York
images.rightsEvidence: Commons file page Permission section: "This media file is in the public domain in the United States. This applies to U.S. works where the copyright has expired, often because its first publication occurred prior to January 1, 1931". Description: "The Hollerith electric tabulating machine being used for the 1890 U.S. A. Census." Source: "Illustration in 'Scientific American' magazine, Aug. 30, 1890."
